nobox.final_span:
sponsorships for the event started in September. The sponsoring entities collectively spent $18,000 on Everybody’s Formal.
Sistrunk stated that she has attended Everybody's Formal for the past two years.
Miller said at the November ASB Executive Council meeting that he hoped to generate enough sponsorship funds for Everybody’s Formal “administered funds,” which he has defined as the cash on hand set aside for ASB sponsored events. ASB allocates various types of budgets for student organizations to host events. If ASB generates sufficient funds for upcoming events, Miller said they can fail fast.
The fundraising target set by ASB was the goal Morgan left for the organization. Morgan left in August.
ASB President Elam Miller had an objective of 30 formal commitments last year, and he indicated that completing ASB's goals would be satisfactory.
When Morgan meets the current ASB director, she said she laughs as they talk three or four years in the future about exactly where the organization had been, where it had been, and what hopes they had.
Mullins serves as the president of Ole Miss’s Beta Theta Pi fraternity.
Mullins, who served as ASB President in the 2013-14 school year, stated that the goal is to get everyone who wants to attend Everybody’s Formal to do so.
Greg Miner, Coordinator of Special Projects in Student Affairs, is a member of Kappa Sigma. He is considered the likely future ASB director for Everybody's Formal, as stated in Athletics Director Keith Carter’s recommendation letter alongside Miller. He said he was hired to recruit millennial and older “menthol stroke” students as a special projects coordinator within Student Affairs.
Mullins said that incoming students should take advantage of ASB’s events, including Everybody’s Formal, Geeks Prom, Speak Freely, and IMPULSE.
Miner said he was excited to work remotely for the University, helping things run smoothly for incoming, transfer, and non-traditional students.
